title: Two laptops edit the same revision
description: Two laptops edit plan.pdf offline, both starting from rev_17. Both upload their changed chunks successfully. The first commits rev_18 before the second asks to commit. You must not silently lose either person's work. What should happen next?

options.text: Pick the edit with the later laptop timestamp and discard the other revision.
options.explanation: Device clocks can be skewed, and even a correct timestamp does not make one person's independent changes disposable.

options.text: Reject the stale baseRev with 409 and let the losing client preserve its uploaded bytes as a conflicted copy.
options.explanation: A conditional revision-pointer update detects the conflict atomically. A sibling file keeps both versions without pretending arbitrary file formats can be merged automatically.

options.text: Change current_rev unconditionally because both chunk uploads were successful.
options.explanation: Durable chunks do not resolve competing metadata commits. An unconditional pointer update silently overwrites the first edit.

options.text: Lock the file from the moment either laptop starts editing until both reconnect.
options.explanation: That is an unbounded lock across offline user activity. Optimistic commits allow useful offline editing while detecting conflicts when they meet.
